name: Dreierschnapsen
summary: Three-player trick-taking bidding game of the Austrian Schnapsen family where one soloist plays against an alliance of two.
rules_text: Played with 20 cards (A,10,K,Q,J in four suits) with German or French suits. Three players receive 6 cards each; 2 cards form the talon. The caller (forehand) chooses trumps from first 3 cards. Then each player may bid a contract; highest contract becomes declarer, with preference to playing without talon and then to seating order. Declarer may exchange with the talon unless he bid without it. Contracts include Rufer (normal game to 66 points), Schnapser (66 in first 4 tricks), Bettler/Plauderer (take no tricks), Gang (take all tricks no trumps) and Bauernschnapser (take all with trumps). Trick play requires following suit and winning if possible, otherwise trumping. King+Queen of a suit can be declared as 20 or 40 points. Winning a contract scores its value; losing gives that value to each defender. First to 24 game points wins the match.
rating_reason: Specific 3p bidding soloist vs alliance with talon
